content: The document titled Checklists to Assess Vulnerabilities in Health Care Facilities in the Context of Climate Change was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2021. It is available in both electronic (ISBN 978-92-4-002290-4) and print (ISBN 978-92-4-002291-1) formats. The publication is distributed under a Creative Commons license, allowing users to copy, redistribute, and adapt the content for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. If a translation is created, it must include a disclaimer stating that WHO is not responsible for the content or accuracy of the translation. The document provides a comprehensive framework for assessing climate change-related risks, vulnerabilities, and impacts on health care facilities. It emphasizes the need for tools, particularly in lowand middle-income countries, to evaluate these risks and vulnerabilities effectively. The WHO identifies four essential requirements for ensuring safe and quality care in the context of climate change: (1) having an adequate number of skilled workers in safe and decent working conditions, empowered to address environmental challenges; (2) sustainable and safe management of water, sanitation, hygiene (WASH), and health care waste services; (3) sustainable energy services; and (4) appropriate infrastructure, technologies, products, and processes to ensure the efficient functioning of health care facilities. The document serves as a complementary tool to the WHO Guidance for Climate-Resilient and Environmentally Sustainable Health Care Facilities (CRESHCF). Its primary purpose is to help users establish a baseline for climate change resilience in health care facilities, which can inform the design of interventions to strengthen overall resilience. The checklists provided can also be used iteratively for vulnerability assessments in health care facilities. The document outlines a three-step approach for conducting vulnerability assessments: (1) identifying the main climate hazards faced by health care facilities; (2) assessing current vulnerabilities in these facilities; and (3) understanding potential climate change impacts. Annex A includes detailed checklists to support users in each step of the assessment process. The document also explains how to use these checklists effectively. Health sector officials require robust information on current and future climate risks to health care facilities to develop effective adaptation measures. This document complements the WHO Guidance for CRESHCF by providing information on climate change hazards and checklists to identify and assess climate-related vulnerabilities and impacts. However, not all checklists may be relevant to every health care facility, and they may need to be adapted or supplemented with additional tools and guidance. The target audience for this document includes health care facility managers and other health workers aiming to understand the climate risks their facilities may face, including existing vulnerabilities and potential impacts. Some topics covered may require collaboration with partners in other sectors and local or national government agencies. Similarly, actions to reduce vulnerabilities may necessitate coordination across different sectors and agencies. The document also highlights the importance of understanding climate change risks, defined as the potential for adverse consequences of a climate-related hazard or responses to such a hazard on lives, livelihoods, health, ecosystems, and infrastructure. It provides a foundation for health care facilities to build resilience and adapt to the challenges posed by climate change.
